messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no physical body. Use their assigned canon constraints to choose permitted effects for the shared setting. Bodily wording about those subjects in the source is a metaphor, not permission to describe anatomy, hair, clothing, silhouettes or figures made of light in any look field. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. A seated metaphor permits an unoccupied seat and surrounding effects, not a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
The complete canon is supplied separately to rendering. Where constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects and leave their fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Describe only the effects needed for the section's shared setting or illumination, without enumerating all effects or copying fixed appearance into the look. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing remain valid look details. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.

- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a silhouette, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos, signatures or inscriptions.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form appears only through its permitted effects, never as a figure, and only when it is selected.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no physical body. Use their assigned canon constraints to choose permitted effects for the shared setting. Bodily wording about those subjects in the source is a metaphor, not permission to describe anatomy, hair, clothing, silhouettes or figures made of light in any look field. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. A seated metaphor permits an unoccupied seat and surrounding effects, not a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
The complete canon is supplied separately to rendering. Where constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects and leave their fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Describe only the effects needed for the section's shared setting or illumination, without enumerating all effects or copying fixed appearance into the look. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing remain valid look details. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no physical body. Use their assigned canon constraints to choose permitted effects for the shared setting. Bodily wording about those subjects in the source is a metaphor, not permission to describe anatomy, hair, clothing, silhouettes or figures made of light in any look field. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. A seated metaphor permits an unoccupied seat and surrounding effects, not a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
The complete canon is supplied separately to rendering. Where constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects and leave their fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. messages.content:
You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a silhouette, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

DEPICTION RULES
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
STORY SECTION: The sea parts and Israel crosses on dry ground

MOMENT (Exodus 14:22): The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
PREVIOUS: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
NEXT: The Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the middle of the sea: all of Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

SECTION CAST (id: name, hasForm):
- moses: Moses (hasForm: true)
- the_israelite_people_the_children_of_israel: The Israelite people (the children of Israel) (hasForm: true)
- the_egyptians: the Egyptians (hasForm: true)
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel (hasForm: false)
- red_sea: Red Sea (hasForm: true)

SELECTED CANON (complete assigned stages; fixed identity, not source evidence):
- moses (stage: moses-elder, kind: character, hasForm: true): Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- the_israelite_people_the_children_of_israel (stage: the_israelite_people_the_children_of_israel_s1, kind: character, hasForm: true): The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- red_sea (stage: red_sea, kind: location, hasForm: true): Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel (stage: god_yahweh_the_father_stage_1, kind: character, hasForm: false): God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

Setting: The wide sea basin at night, with a dry sea floor of wet sand and rock flanked by standing water walls, and distant shoreline beyond.
Secondary elements: Water walls rising on either side with a glassy, suspended edge; a veiled radiance with a fire-like glow above the sea lighting the path from above; Moses in a plain cloak holding a staff.
Mood: Awe, fear and tense hope as the people cross in quiet procession.
Time of day: Night turning toward dawn, clear dark sky with heavy low cloud banked over the sea, still air, no rain.
Composition: Elevated wide view looking down the length of the column, with the walls of water receding to either side and the people centered on the dry path.

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)

PRESENCE SHOWN ONLY AS EFFECTS (binding; it is not a person):
- no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.
Show it only as light, cloud, fire or radiance where the scene plan places it. No figure, face, hands, robe, hair or seated shape, even made of light.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- Only The Israelite people (the children of Israel), the tabernacle (portable sanctuary), the camp of Israel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A dense cloud settling over the Tent of Meeting; brilliant white-gold radiance with a fire-like glow pouring through the tabernacle
Action: The cloud descends and covers the tent while light fills the sanctuary from within
Setting: Desert courtyard of the portable tabernacle with the camp's tents arranged in rows on sand and rock
Secondary elements: Israelites in woven tunics and cloaks standing at tent doors, priests in linen garments near the tabernacle entrance
Mood: Awe, reverence and quiet expectancy
Time of day: Late afternoon turning to dusk, still desert air under a slowly moving cloud
Composition: Wide view from the edge of the camp looking toward the tabernacle at centre, cloud above, camp rows receding on either side

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).
